monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster average pace and higher HR — indicating a meaningful shift toward more demanding aerobic work. Efficiency and cadence have also improved, suggesting better neuromuscular coordination.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved from 13.42 to 13.62 m/sec per bpm — the largest positive shift among all metrics — reflecting better oxygen utilization per heartbeat at given paces.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s distance by 5.5 km and need only one more run to match last month’s session count. No additional volume is required — prioritize quality and recovery over adding runs.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.62 even as avg HR increased from 136 to 140 bpm — meaning you’re moving farther per heartbeat at faster paces, likely due to improved lactate buffering and running economy.

insights.title: Shift toward higher-intensity work
insights.body: Zone 3 time jumped from 19% to 29%, and Zone 4 from 3% to 15% — a +12 percentage point increase in threshold+ work — while Z1+Z2 dropped from 79% to 54%. This signals intentional progression but risks under-recovery if Z1/Z2 volume falls too low.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff stabilized
insights.body: Cadence increased +5 spm (146 → 151) while stride length remained consistent (~69 cm on long runs) and ground contact time stayed ~314–317 ms — indicating improved turnover without sacrificing power or posture, especially evident in your three 10+ km runs.

insights.title: High aerobic TE on long efforts
insights.body: Your 11.1 km run on 2026-06-07 and 11.0 km on 2026-06-16 both delivered aerobic TE of 3.4–3.6 — well above your monthly average of 2.6 — confirming effective stimulus for central adaptations, but note that no Z1/Z2 recovery runs appear in the recent log (last Z1/Z2 run was 2026-06-19 at 112 bpm, TE=1.6).

recommendations.action: Do a 45-minute Zone 2 run (HR 128–135 bpm) on your next easy day, keeping cadence ≥148 spm and pace no faster than 9:30 min/km.
recommendations.reason: Your Z1/Z2 share dropped to 54% this month (vs 79% last month), and your most recent easy run (2026-06-19) had low TE (1.6) but high ground contact (344 ms) — signaling need for true recovery stimulus to restore neuromuscular freshness.

recommendations.action: Add 2x 60-second strides (90–95% effort) after your next moderate run, focusing on quick turnover (cadence ≥165 spm) and minimal vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm).
recommendations.reason: Your fastest recent run (2026-06-11) hit 162 spm and 8.4 cm vertical oscillation — slightly elevated vs your typical 7.7 cm — suggesting opportunity to reinforce efficient form at speed.

recommendations.action: Perform a 5-minute post-run mobility routine targeting hip flexors and calves immediately after your next run, especially following any session with ground contact >315 ms (e.g., your 10.5 km on 2026-06-21 had 314 ms).
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time has trended upward on longer runs (314–317 ms), correlating with subtle fatigue; mobility helps maintain elastic recoil and stride spring.

weekly_focus.description: Balance your recent gains in threshold capacity with deliberate low-HR stimulus and form reinforcement — ensuring adaptations consolidate without accumulating residual fatigue.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 endurance run (45 min, HR ≤135 bpm)
Moderate-long run (10 km, HR 138–142 bpm, cadence ≥150 spm)
Strides + mobility session (3 km easy + 2x60s strides + 5-min mobility)
